Making sampling differentiable by setting α=ϕz. To
train our model, we need to backpropagate gradients into
the probabilities of the depth buckets ϕ. This means we
need to compute the derivatives ∇ϕµof the mean µwith
respect to probabilities ϕ. Unfortunately, the sampling oper-
ation z∼pϕ(z)is not differentiable. Inspired by variational
autoencoders [ 21], we overcome this challenge via a repa-
rameterization trick. Accordingly, we set the opacity αof
a Gaussian to be equal to the probability of the bucket that
it was sampled from. Consider that we sampled z∼pϕ(z).
We then set α=ϕz, i.e., we set αto the z-th entry of the
vector of probabilities ϕ. This means that in each backward
pass, we assign the gradients of the loss Lwith respect to the
opacities αto the gradients of the depth probability buckets
ϕ, i.e.,∇ϕL=∇αL.
